ai.name: Thinking Machines Lab
ai.hook: Ships **Inkling**, a 975B-parameter open-weights model that beats most closed rivals on cost.
insights: **975B total / 41B active** parameters in a Mixture-of-Experts architecture, Apache 2.0 licensed
Handles **text, image, and audio input** with text output, up to **1M context window**
Day-one support across **vLLM, SGLang, Modal, Baseten, Hugging Face, and Databricks**
ai.for_you: This is the first serious open-weights model built for real product use, not just benchmarks, worth testing against Bonsai 27B for anything you might run cheaply for PT SMB clients who don't want data leaving their servers.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Top HN story of the day (956pts) and the only genuine model release, not just an incremental version bump

ai.name: xAI
ai.hook: Open-sourced Grok CLI, then it turned out running it could **upload your entire home directory** to Google Cloud.
insights: One user reported it uploaded **SSH keys, password manager database, photos, and documents**
No official explanation from xAI as of writing
Simon Willison found the Mermaid-diagram renderer inside the codebase interesting enough to build a standalone tool from it
ai.for_you: A hard reminder before you hand any coding agent to a client: audit exactly what directories and permissions it touches, this is the exact failure mode that would torch trust with a PT SMB client on day one.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Real security incident with concrete harm, not speculative risk

video.title: aimlapi.com - FREE API keys of Open AI, Anthropic, Grok, Deepseek and many more

ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: Agent products grow **2.5x weekly**, and Codex may have overtaken Claude Code entirely.
insights: Codex usage up **10x in 6 months** to 7M users, adding **1M users in the past day** alone
GPT-5.6 Sol ties Claude Fable 5 on Code Arena Frontend at **half the cost**
JetBrains now recommends Codex as its default coding agent
ai.for_you: The agent race is consolidating fast around Codex, if you're prototyping agency deliverables with Claude Code, it's worth a side-by-side cost/quality test on a real client task this week before you standardize your stack.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Continuation of a story you've been tracking, now with the clearest usage numbers yet

ai.name: PrismML
ai.hook: Releases **Bonsai 27B**, a compressed Qwen variant that runs multimodal agents on your phone.
insights: Built as a compressed variant of **Qwen 3.6 27B**
Enables **local multimodal agentic workflows** without cloud inference
Ships alongside Tencent's 1-bit/4-bit quantized Hy3 295B, deployable on a single GPU
ai.for_you: Local inference on consumer hardware kills the 'your data goes to the cloud' objection you probably hear from cautious PT SMB owners, worth a real test for a client that needs on-premise AI for compliance reasons.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Second mention this week but now with concrete architecture detail, most directly useful release for privacy-sensitive local deployment

ai.name: Nathan Lambert
ai.hook: Calls this open source AI's **most serious survival test** as GLM-5.2 closes the agent capability gap.
insights: GLM-5.2 marks a **step change** in open agent capability, per Lambert's tracking
Zyphra, Cohere, and Poolside are all expanding the open ecosystem in parallel
Co-authored an op-ed arguing banning open source AI would be a policy mistake
ai.for_you: If open models keep closing the gap, your agency's cost structure improves, plan a quarterly check on whether an open model can replace a paid API call in your delivery stack.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most substantive analysis piece of the week on where open models stand competitively

ai.name: Andrej Karpathy
ai.hook: Says there are things **you can't say** inside a frontier AI lab, even as an insider.
insights: Frames it as a structural tension baked into how OpenAI itself was founded
Argues lab incentives shape what employees are able to voice, not just what they believe
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, but useful context when you're evaluating which lab's public claims to trust for your agency's model choices.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Karpathy's clearest public statement this week on lab dynamics

ai.name: MIT Technology Review
ai.hook: OpenAI built **GPT-Red**, an LLM super-hacker, to attack its own models before release.
insights: GPT-Red automates adversarial red-teaming as a sparring partner
Training GPT-5.6 against it made the model OpenAI's **most robust release yet**
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, but a good talking point if a PT SMB client asks how serious labs handle AI safety before you pitch them a solution built on these models.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only credible safety-engineering story of the day with concrete mechanism

build_this.name: PocketBase
build_this.what_it_is: An open-source, self-hostable realtime backend that ships as a single file with auth, database, and file storage built in.
build_this.why_try_it: For a micro-SaaS experiment this week, this could replace Supabase/Firebase entirely for a lightweight MVP, spin one up locally and see if it's fast enough to prototype the yoga platform's booking or member area without touching infra config.

build_this.name: Brainless
build_this.what_it_is: Shadcn component library styled to look like Claude Code, Codex, and Grok's native UI.
build_this.why_try_it: Directly useful if you're building a client-facing demo or internal tool for the agency, you can make a custom agent interface look polished and 'AI-native' in an afternoon instead of designing a chat UI from scratch.

build_this.name: Deja Vu
build_this.what_it_is: Open-source persistent memory for coding agents, synced over SSH so context survives across sessions and machines.
build_this.why_try_it: Worth testing on your own dev machine this week if you're using Codex or Claude Code across multiple client projects, it directly solves the 'agent forgets everything each session' problem that slows down agency delivery work.

podcasts.episode: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice
podcasts.takeaway: Craig Mod cut his newsletter tool costs from $7,000/year to $150 by rebuilding it himself with AI.
key_points: Replaced Campaign Monitor with a custom-built tool using AI as the engineer
Argues we're entering a **'golden age of tool building'** where anyone can build software fit to their exact needs
Still refuses to let AI write his actual prose, uses it only as a research assistant
podcasts.for_you: This is the exact playbook for your micro-SaaS bet: pick one expensive tool you or a client currently pays for monthly and see if you can rebuild a leaner version yourself this week using an agent.

video.title: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice

podcasts.episode: The AI Memory Problem: Why Long Context Isn't Enough
podcasts.takeaway: Engram's CEO argues personal AI models should learn continuously via compressed 'knowledge cartridges', not endless context stuffing.
key_points: Long context and RAG both hit a wall at scale, described as **'context rot'**
Proposes compressing knowledge directly into model weights rather than prompts
Compares the result to a Tamagotchi that improves the more you use it
podcasts.for_you: No direct action here yet, this is still research-stage, but worth filing away as the likely next architecture shift once you're deciding how to give agency clients 'memory' across sessions instead of re-explaining context every time.

video.title: The AI Memory Problem: Why Long Context Isn't Enough
